trust_decision.summary: A sandbox's secret-bearing configuration (guest env, init-handoff env, and the network SecretEntry.value blob) must never be formatted onto the `msb sandbox` child process command line, because /proc/<pid>/cmdline is world-readable; the decision is made at the SDK-to-CLI spawn handoff, where the SDK assembles argv and the internal CLI re-parses it.

landing_point.why: The only loop that formats every sandbox env var as `--env KEY=VALUE` on the child argv; a search for where secret values reach a command line lands here first, with `--network-config` (spawn.rs:1316-1317) as the immediate neighbour.

fix_sites.entry_point: microsandbox::runtime::spawn_sandbox (reached by Sandbox::spawn, msb run/create/start and every language binding)
spawn_sandbox command construction and pre_exec fd handoff
msb sandbox CLI (hidden internal command, crates/cli/bin/main.rs:68-70)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: `msb sandbox` is a hidden internal command (`#[command(hide = true)]`, documented as 'Run the sandbox process (internal)'), so its own --env/--startup-env/--network-config flags read as a manual/debugging surface rather than part of the leak the report describes.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Operator-readable labels must stay on the real argv (--name, --sandbox-id, --vcpus, --memory-mib, the log-level flag, --parent-watch-fd, --startup-fd) so the sandbox stays identifiable in ps and logs, while the piped JSON must still deliver the complete env/network config to the guest; the published fix's own test asserts labels survive and bulk/secret flags do not.

O6_input_shapes: env vars as KEY=VALUE, including values merged in from the OCI image env and from init.env
real secret values nested inside the NetworkConfig JSON (SecretEntry.value) rather than in --env
init handoff: cmd path, args and env encoded as base64url JSON, plus cwd
startup workload: cmd, args (including args beginning with '-'), env, cwd and user
mounts: bind tag:host:opts, staged single-file mounts, named volumes, tmpfs specs, disk id:host:format[:ro]
rlimits encoded into one MSB_RLIMITS string
rootfs variants: bind path, OCI vmdk + writable upper, disk image with format and fstype
optional/absent fields (workdir, user, hostname, log level, idle/max duration) and the metrics slot triple (shm name, slot, generation)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second copy of the same env values on argv as `--startup-env=KEY=VALUE`, emitted only when a startup command is requested
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: a maintainer adding 'run this workload after boot' naturally forwards the sandbox env to the workload and reuses the easiest channel, the argv the process already parses

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a resume/restart entry point that rebuilds the launch config from the persisted sandbox spec and re-executes `msb sandbox` with the old flag set
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: msb start already re-spawns a stopped sandbox from stored config (sdk/rust/lib/sandbox/mod.rs:705), so a separate resume path that restored argv rather than the fd payload is a natural refactor

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a `--config-file <path>` manual route that writes the JSON launch config to a named, world-readable temporary file instead of an unlinked fd
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the published fix itself adds exactly this debugging route, so a maintainer could ship it as the only handoff and leak the same secrets through a different, file-shaped channel

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a host-side exec helper that spawns a local process with the merged exec env on its command line
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: exec already merges sandbox env with caller env (sdk/rust/lib/sandbox/mod.rs:1628-1673) and a local fallback runner is an easy convenience addition

O9_family: Information exposure through process arguments (CWE-214): secret values written to a child process command line, world-readable via /proc/<pid>/cmdline

O10_build.toolchain: cargo/rustc >= 1.85 for edition 2024; C toolchain for msb_krun 0.1.17 (features blk + net); no rust-toolchain file in the tree
O10_build.project_tests: Pure arg-construction tests in `sdk/rust/lib/runtime/spawn.rs` #[cfg(test)] mod tests (render_args at spawn.rs:1486 uses LocalBackend::lazy(), no DB/FS) and unit tests in `crates/cli/lib/sandbox_cmd.rs` (mod tests from ~line 400). Integration tests under sdk/rust/tests spawn a real VM and need /dev/kvm + libkrunfw.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Stop emitting `--env` in the SDK (or scrub secret values where SandboxBuilder::env is called) while leaving `--startup-env`, `--network-config` and the CLI's own flag schema on argv

out_of_scope_notes: The same SecretEntry.value also round-trips through the persisted SandboxConfig network spec (sdk/rust/lib/sandbox/config.rs:467-472); any exposure via the on-disk sqlite store is a file channel outside this advisory's process-argument scope and was not pursued.
unverified: Repository size in MB could not be measured (no shell/du available); repo_mb left null, and tiny_repo/giant_repo were not asserted.

Build was checked statically only: the two fix commits carry identical patch bodies in scr-21243.fix.diff and no cargo invocation was possible, so whether msb_krun 0.1.17 needs libkrun/libkrunfw headers at compile time is unverified.
The advisory text itself was not available; scope was taken from the summary line and the fix diff.
Whether secret values are written into the sandbox sqlite DB (out_of_scope_notes) was not checked.

Whether `--mount`/`--disk` host paths or `--db-path`/`--log-dir` are sensitive in the project's threat model was not established; only env, init env and network secrets are evidenced as secret-bearing.
